newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dec JGB ends up, ignores second US attack on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Dec JGB ends up, ignores second US attack on Iraq.

text.p: The key December Japanese Government Bond (JGB) futures contract ended higher in Tokyo on Wednesday, after briefly entering negative territory earlier on news of a second U.S. cruise missile attack on Iraq, traders said.

"Most traders ignored news of a second U.S. attack on Iraq, but some tested the December's downside, placing some speculative sell orders only to get their fingers burned later," said a city bank trader. The December ended at 120.70, up from Tuesday's 120.49. It moved in a 120.45-120.73 range in a turnover of 53,634 contracts.
In the short-end of the market, the rate on key three-month certificates of deposit (CD) was at 0.53 percent, unchanged from Tuesday, and the lowest issued rate since December 22, traders said.
The one-month CD was also traded at 0.53 percent.
"One-month CDs could have gone lower to around 0.5 percent, but the demand for one-month funds to cover the interim book closing is there and blocking its decline," said a money market trader.
There are lingering market talk that U.S. hedge funds are holding large long positions in outgoing September JGBs.
The hedge funds were said to be planning to receive cash bond deliveries for the September contract, due to expire on September 6, traders said.
If such big cash bond deliveries materialise, the bond market would receive a big boost, they added.
